batch_strategy: Use recent failures to choose local response and loading comparisons, then test the structural boundaries of those corrections. Measure selected prediction reversals without imposing universal monotonicity. Include one targeted repeat to assess reproducibility of the newly observed loading-solvent association.

choices.reason: p-Methylbenzyl alcohol m135 at 2/1 and 98 mg bridges the same-loading 1/1 record 4d08b9494002d348513d, measured at 9.82/15.28 mL, to the recent 5/1 record 716d04ed1943f0708912 at 20.92/34.02. The latter had a 19.31 mL historical completion underprediction. This bridge localizes where the larger alcohol response begins.

Bromobenzyl alcohol m207 at 5/1 and 78 mg tests the lower-loading boundary of the unusually compact 156 mg result ec6846c0fcb7df17c97d, measured at 4.89/10.42 mL. Its paired 10/1 experiment will determine whether the sharp solvent response persists at this mass.

m207 at 10/1 and 78 mg completes the lower-loading solvent pair. The 156 mg record ff3b6b1069b7d66ad021 measured 38.08/66.27 mL after substantial underprediction. This label tests whether that correction transfers across loading while preserving the compact 5/1 region.

m207 at 5/1 and 234 mg supplies the upper-loading side of a rectangle around the measured 156 mg solvent pair. The current prediction changes little with mass. Measurement tests whether the compact 5/1 association is sustained across loading or confined to the existing record.

m207 at 10/1 and 234 mg completes the rectangle with the selected 78 mg and 5/1 experiments. Together with ec6846c0fcb7df17c97d and ff3b6b1069b7d66ad021, it distinguishes a broadly reproducible solvent transition from a loading-dependent response in either endpoint.

Bromopropionic acid m45 at 10/1 and 85 mg directly contrasts with d43d692e19100ebe5646 at 170 mg, measured at 14.79/32.17 mL. The recent 85 mg 20/1 record b24f66ff77974f8ba6e1 measured 39.58/65.65, substantially later than the 170 mg anchor. This point tests whether the large loading association emerges only in weaker eluent.

m45 at 50/1 and 170 mg extends the exact-loading curve from d43d692e19100ebe5646 at 10/1 and e6605c23fb1943a6b848 at 20/1. It tests how the acid response continues beyond the loading-sensitive region, constraining weak-eluent transfer without inferring unrecorded pH or concentration.

Repeat the recorded m92 EA-loaded 1/1 condition at 57.75 mg and 200 uL. The recent record 95a3dcfe4436e929aa30 finished at 11.70 mL, versus 20.57 for its PE-loaded match e626b5b8083ea1fd02f2. Exact-condition EA-loaded 2/1 records 9768d61b571fc0c5ce1a and 6cd3f929d7d90a9c29b3 also differ. This targeted repeat assesses reproducibility before spreading a solvent correction.

Methyl phenylglyoxylate m92 at 5/1 and 57.75 mg with EA/200 uL loading tests the solvent-strength scope of the recent low-loading 1/1 result 95a3dcfe4436e929aa30. Higher-loading EA records 6c1c34b12c66ebcf39a4 and 4b8ba288d549f6cfc94b provide 5/1 and 10/1 context. This separates a localized strong-eluent association from a response extending further along the curve.

m9 at 5/1 and 67.6 mg with DCM/300 uL loading differs only in recorded loading solvent from measured PE-loaded record 36e3d917ed07cf327a84. The model predicts a small difference. This exact comparison tests loading-solvent transfer into a nonpolar biphenyl scaffold after the much larger glyoxylate association.

m9 at 50/1 and 67.6 mg with PE/300 uL loading forms an exact solvent comparison with DCM-loaded f3f7cfc40e5b84b18566, measured at 6.08/11.77 mL. Together with the selected 5/1 DCM row and its measured PE match, it tests whether the loading-solvent association changes with mobile-phase strength.

o-Methoxyacetophenone m127 at 50/1 and 109 mg tests a predicted completion decrease from the same-loading 20/1 measurement 15d6bc57a87392fbeb98, 31.71 mL, to about 27.54 mL. Lower-loading records 8143c4fff6f999b7ad0e and 52b9af4df1f1e7cd4d9b already show a measured 20/1-to-50/1 decrease, so this is a transfer test rather than an assumed monotonicity violation.

m127 at 50/1 and 163.5 mg completes the selected weak-eluent loading comparison and matches ebdeaba52880c7eade16 at 20/1, measured at 5.08/31.97 mL. The current 50/1 completion prediction is almost identical to that at 109 mg. These labels test whether the recorded weak-eluent decrease survives at higher masses and whether onset needs a separate loading response.

Fused ether-aldehyde m194 at 1/1 and 58.85 mg bounds the stronger-eluent side of recent records 2bd4f8787a951ef0ee04 and c393010c592b487413e2 at 2/1 and 5/1. Both recent completions were overpredicted by more than 11 mL at acquisition. This label tests how far that local correction should extend; its current completion prediction exceeds the measured 2/1 value.

m194 at 2/1 and 117.7 mg fills the loading midpoint between 2bd4f8787a951ef0ee04 at 58.85 mg, measured at 5.93/14.73 mL, and 2bb48a2862bf80c30a36 at 176.55 mg, 4.63/28.18. This unusually large completion association contrasts with the lactone's nearly unchanged 10/1 completion across loading and can teach endpoint-specific interactions.

Tetralone m180 at 10/1 and 109.9 mg bridges exact-loading records 73a35f890e678b320073 at 5/1 and 1668026caa5d708642cf at 20/1. Comparison with m179's measured 10/1-to-50/1 curve tests the location of ring-environment differences after the recent seven-membered ketone labels limited transfer of the lactone correction.

Acetylnaphthalene m40 at 10/1 and 56 mg starts a fixed-loading extension from 551ec1f8caaa42f2e478 at 2/1, measured at 7.07/13.21 mL. It tests whether the larger weak-eluent response of acetylfluorene, established by 86fb9a8fd6633397d670 and cace6f00c46aea69fe39 under different loading conditions, transfers to this aromatic environment.

m40 at 50/1 and 56 mg completes the selected 10/1-to-50/1 pair. Predicted completion is about 31.76 mL. The pair can establish a meaningful boundary between external aromatic acetyl groups, fused ketones and the much steeper measured lactone curve, with scaffold differences treated as hypotheses rather than mechanisms established by the data.

Methylenedioxy acetophenone m39 at 10/1 and 100 mg fills an intermediate response point beyond same-loading 1/1 record 162ffd9b0db1fd3c1509. Records ae8805bc02bce03072e2 and a6a0404c3ad65c6d9326 establish a substantial 5/1-to-20/1 increase at 150 mg. This label tests transfer across loading near that transition; its high CW distance supplies additional coverage evidence.

Methoxy-substituted ethyl benzoate m87 at 2/1 and 165.45 mg supplies the stronger-eluent side of a local curve with the selected 5/1 point and measured 10/1 record ef809aee1c6b06021475. The pair tests an ether-ester connectivity that should not automatically inherit corrections from ether-ketones or aminoesters.

m87 at 5/1 and 165.45 mg predicts completion near 24.26 mL, above the same-loading 10/1 measurement ef809aee1c6b06021475 at 21.79. Measuring this point alongside 2/1 distinguishes a local maximum from interpolation error. Recorded 5/1-to-10/1 decreases in para-methoxyacetophenone provide a reason to test, rather than rule out, this shape.

Hydroxy-methoxybenzaldehyde m117 at 2/1 and 182.145 mg begins a matched stronger-eluent shape experiment. Its current completion prediction, about 17.42 mL, exceeds the selected 5/1 prediction. Same-loading 20/1 record 7e834c7b870ef7024d35 supplies a measured weaker-eluent boundary for this donor-plus-acceptor environment.

m117 at 5/1 and 182.145 mg completes the selected pair. Record c68db037670dea886720 measures 5/1 at 60.715 mg, while 7e834c7b870ef7024d35 measures 20/1 at the selected mass. This label tests both the predicted local completion decrease and the extent of stronger-eluent loading transfer.

Branched-chain acrylate m16 at 5/1 and 88.5 mg starts a matched comparison in an underconstrained monoester region. The model predicts greater completion here than at the selected 20/1 condition. Record 97fe38c6942b67ea70b2 establishes compact 50/1 elution at 44.25 mg; the latest lauryl-acrylate labels further motivate testing a shallow response boundary.

m16 at 20/1 and 88.5 mg completes the selected pair, with predicted completion decreasing from about 13.53 to 10.88 mL. Measurement tests whether this is recorded response heterogeneity or an interpolation artifact, and helps prevent steep corrections learned from multifunctional acrylates from spreading into simple monoesters.

Methyl mercaptoacetate m96 at 50/1 and 59.35 mg forms an exact loading comparison with 18aafc3a2522f8cc2983, measured at 26.48/40.64 mL at 178.05 mg. The current model varies little with mass. This extends loading learning to a thiol-containing monoester, where donor presence alone cannot determine the acid-, alcohol- or ether-aldehyde-like association.

Thioether benzaldehyde m129 in pure EA at 114.4 mg starts a stronger-eluent pair. Same-loading 2/1 record e05652bb38d9efd5b11e measured 6.00/12.38 mL, whereas the current pure-EA prediction has later onset and slightly later completion. This tests the stronger-eluent boundary of a sulfur-containing neutral acceptor scaffold.

m129 at 1/1 and 114.4 mg completes the selected strong-eluent pair and predicts 8.94/14.76 mL, above the measured 2/1 response e05652bb38d9efd5b11e. Records cf8ab33c25ad391a584c and 4c46ceefd6147b1e0a7a anchor 5/1 and 10/1. This local check limits transfer from the much larger thioether-ketone response.

Dimethyl acetylenedicarboxylate m91 at 5/1 and 141.2 mg starts a matched shallow-response check, extending the exact-loading 2/1 measurement d603d4af5fd62fa8b85e at 5.62/7.98 mL. This diester remained comparatively compact in measured stronger-eluent records despite four acceptors, making it a useful boundary against acceptor-count-based overcorrection.

m91 at 20/1 and 141.2 mg completes the selected pair. The predicted completion is about 9.96 mL, below the 5/1 prediction of 11.86. Record 48679ae48dd485ffb7a6 provides 50/1 context at 211.8 mg. The pair tests whether the apparent flattening or decrease is reproducible while learning a sparsely measured alkyne-diester response.

Methyl mandelate m99 at 1/1 and 150 mg with DCM/1000 uL loading begins an exact-condition solvent-response pair. Predicted completion is 19.53 mL, above the selected 2/1 prediction. Record 7bbdec21c428010dd67b anchors 10/1 at the same loading conditions, so the pair can locate where the hydroxyester response begins without assuming a donor-wide correction.

m99 at 2/1 and 150 mg completes the selected pair, predicted at 9.88/14.62 mL. Lower-loading 2/1 record 30456dafbfe681b5af70 measured 11.57/15.78, and 8e701efd2ee4729edc4b anchors 5/1 at 50 mg. This label tests the predicted completion dip and constrains loading transfer in the large recorded loading-volume regime.

hypotheses.content: Loading associations depend on scaffold, eluent and endpoint. The latest acid comparison shows much later onset and completion at lower loading at 20/1. The lactone's 10/1 completion changes little across loading, while the fused ether-aldehyde's 2/1 completion changes substantially. A common loading correction would obscure these differences.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched comparisons can teach endpoint-specific loading interactions and establish where their transfer across solvent regimes or functional groups fails.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the acid's lower-loading association already appear at 10/1, does the ether-aldehyde loading midpoint interpolate, and what association holds for the thiol monoester at 50/1?

hypotheses.content: Neutral acceptor-containing scaffolds have connectivity-dependent condition responses. The latest seven-membered fused ketone grows much less at weak eluent than the lactone, and its previous predictions overextended that response. The ether-aldehyde's stronger-eluent completions were also overpredicted. Structural explanations remain chemical priors; the measurements establish boundaries rather than adsorption mechanisms.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Response bridges and chemically related boundaries can localize corrections instead of propagating large weak-eluent retention increases across every carbonyl or ether-containing molecule.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which transition shapes transfer to acetylnaphthalene, methylenedioxy acetophenone and tetralone, and how far should the ether-aldehyde's stronger-eluent correction extend?

hypotheses.content: Benzylic alcohols have distinct transition locations and recorded local shapes. p-Methylbenzyl alcohol already has substantial retention at 5/1 and grows further at 10/1. Bromobenzyl alcohol instead has a compact 5/1 record below its measured 2/1 response, followed by a large 10/1 increase. The brominated scaffold's dip may reflect a reproducible condition association or record heterogeneity; its mechanism is unestablished.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The methylbenzyl bridge and bromobenzyl loading rectangle distinguish transition-location errors from loading-dependent responses, limiting donor-only generalization.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where does the methylbenzyl increase begin, and does bromobenzyl alcohol preserve compact 5/1 elution and large 10/1 growth at both lower and higher loading?

hypotheses.content: Early onset and modest completion growth need separate constraints in weakly interacting regions. Indene's latest 10/1 and 50/1 completions are nearly equal, and lauryl acrylate's measured 1/1 and 5/1 endpoints are ordered and compact. Their results support a local boundary against excessive polar-scaffold corrections, while the current branched-acrylate and alkyne-diester response shapes remain untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These measurements constrain lower-retention portions of the Row-distribution while allowing real completion-volume variation and local reversals.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the predicted completion decreases in branched acrylate and dimethyl acetylenedicarboxylate present in matched measurements?

hypotheses.content: Prediction reversals require local evidence. The latest o-methoxyacetophenone and trimethoxybenzene 2/1-to-5/1 completion decreases disappeared in measurement. Dibenzylideneacetone's pronounced pure-EA onset warning also disappeared, although its measured completion still exceeds the 1/1 value. Conversely, lower-loading o-methoxyacetophenone has a measured 20/1-to-50/1 decrease, and para-methoxyacetophenone has measured 5/1-to-10/1 decreases. These findings favor scaffold- and condition-specific shape learning.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched checks distinguish interpolation artifacts from recorded nonmonotonic associations, repairing local predictions without erasing genuine response heterogeneity.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the current m87, m117, m129 and m99 strong-eluent reversals occur in measurements, and does m127's weak-eluent completion decrease persist at higher loadings?

hypotheses.content: At methyl phenylglyoxylate, PE/EA 1/1, 57.75 mg and 200 uL loading volume, the measured EA-loaded record has earlier onset and lower completion than the PE-loaded record by about 2.30 and 8.87 mL. This is a recorded association, not yet a reproducible or general causal solvent effect. Variation between exact-condition EA-loaded 2/1 records warrants a targeted repeat and limits confidence in broad transfer.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Reproducibility and exact loading-solvent comparisons can identify an important condition-feature interaction while preventing a single unusual label from producing a global solvent offset.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the EA-loaded 1/1 result reproduce, how does its low-loading response continue at 5/1, and are PE-versus-DCM associations small or condition-dependent in the nonpolar m9 scaffold?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes shift emphasis toward local boundaries and reproducibility. m135's 5/1 and 10/1 measurements substantially exceeded acquisition predictions, rejecting the proposed compact 5/1 region for that scaffold. m207 instead measured a very compact 5/1 response and a large 10/1 response, with opposite error directions at acquisition. I therefore choose a methylbenzyl bridge and a bromobenzyl loading rectangle instead of applying a uniform alcohol increase. The acid's new 85 mg 20/1 record revealed a much larger lower-loading association than predicted; its 10/1 loading comparison now becomes particularly informative. The lactone's 20/1 bridge was overpredicted by roughly 8–9 mL, while its lower-loading 10/1 label was predicted closely. Together with the moderate measured m179 curve, this limits extension of the earlier lactone 50/1 correction and motivates selective structural boundaries. Ethyl anthranilate's 10/1 bridge and the phenylpyridine 5/1 loading pair were comparatively well predicted, reducing the priority of adjacent nitrogen-scaffold rows this round. The m127 and m110 predicted stronger-eluent completion maxima were not supported by measurement. However, m164 retained a smaller measured completion reversal, and other measured curves also decrease locally, so I continue selective shape checks without imposing a universal monotonicity rule. Indene's completion nearly plateaued from 10/1 to 50/1, and lauryl acrylate supplied ordinary, compact endpoints where the model had predicted an endpoint reversal. These findings strengthen the need to protect weakly interacting regions from excessive retention corrections. Finally, the exact glyoxylate loading-solvent pair showed a substantially larger association than predicted, with EA loading producing lower completion rather than the predicted higher completion. Existing exact-condition variability motivates one repeat before generalizing that association. All errors discussed here are acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The 32 experiments span 17 scaffolds. Repeated molecules serve explicit scientific comparisons: the bromobenzyl rectangle tests solvent-response transfer across loading; acid, ether-aldehyde and thiol-ester comparisons constrain different endpoint-specific loading associations; and the m9 comparisons isolate loading solvent at two mobile-phase strengths. One glyoxylate repeat assesses whether the latest large solvent association is reproducible, while its 5/1 extension tests the association's condition scope. Carbonyl and ether-containing response bridges establish transfer boundaries around recent failures, including the moderate fused-ketone response and the steep lactone and acetylfluorene curves. Selected local shape checks address current interpolation warnings in ester, hydroxyester, aldehyde and methoxy-carbonyl environments where measured reversals prevent a universal monotonicity assumption. Branched acrylate and the alkyne diester constrain comparatively compact regions that could otherwise inherit excessive retention corrections. These comparisons can improve generalization by teaching where corrections should begin, which endpoint they affect and where structural or loading transfer should stop. CW distance provides supplementary coverage evidence; single-predictor quantile spans are not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and V2 minus V1 remains an elution interval. Unrecorded factors and record heterogeneity limit causal interpretation. All 32 IDs are fixed together, and their premeasurement predictions are the exact supplied candidate-table values identified by this packet hash.
